payload.explanation: Monitor mon_b5b4c1731e46 (effort_event on finger_joint, threshold le 10 per u_brown's contract clause invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous / registry max_clamp_effort=10) fired at trigger_wall_ns=1791600075885470500 with triggering_value=24.11. get_evidence over 1791600074e9-1791600078e9 on joint_states/finger_joint shows effort near zero (~-0.02) through the approach, then during grasp_skill's close motion it ramps from ~-0.009 at pos 0.578 to 24.1 at pos 0.597, climbing further to a sustained plateau of ~57.69 by pos 0.6328 (gripper fully closed) and holding there for the rest of the window. This is not a brief contact-chatter spike: it is a sustained plateau at ~5.8x the part's tolerated clamp effort (10), consistent with the gripper closing past the point of first contact and continuing to squeeze u_brown well beyond its rated clamp force -- an overclamp on a part whose spec sets a tight 10-unit limit (unusually low relative to u_orange/line_green/inverted_u_yellow, which tolerate 200/170/250). I did not dismiss this as plausible contact noise because the value never relaxes back toward the floor; it stays pinned at 57.69 for the remainder of the evidence window, which is the signature of continued clamping force rather than a transient. Clause invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous is violated.

Monitor mon_b6769180c91a (effort_event, finger_joint, le 10 per u_brown's contract invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous) fired again at trigger_wall_ns=1791600128204944100 with triggering_value=50.85, well above the 10-unit limit. This is the continuation of the same overclamp condition first recorded under step pick_u_brown: the gripper closed on u_brown to a sustained plateau around 57.7 during the pick, and that clamp force has not relaxed while the arm transits toward place_approach_u_brown. I am recording it under this step_id per instructions (fire scoped to the step it occurs in), but it is the same standing violation, not a new independent event; no new mechanism is inferred beyond the overclamp already characterized at pick time.

payload.explanation: Milestone check at place_u_brown close, evaluated against u_brown's own evidence, not the executor's claim. (1) Standing invariant invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous (le 10, from registry max_clamp_effort) remained violated throughout this step: get_evidence on finger_joint from 1791600142e9-1791600158e9 shows effort held at ~48-52 the entire time u_brown was gripped and carried, continuing the overclamp first caught at pick_u_brown and already flagged at place_approach_u_brown; no new mechanism, same standing violation, recorded here because the clause is due at every step covering invariants and the breach was still live through end of this step. (2) object_lift_height_m: u_brown's pose rose from a resting z=0.0398 to a lift plateau z=0.2396 (object_poses evidence, pick->transit window), a rise of ~0.200 m, well over the 0.05 m floor -- pass. (3) object_tcp_offset_m: the relative_frame monitor armed at grasp (mon_7483a151d818, parent=tcp, child=u_brown) captured a reference translation magnitude of ~0.0912 m at grasp time and never fired through the entire carry (max_delta_m=0.02); recomputing the same tcp-to-u_brown distance from object_poses/frames evidence at the end of the lift gives ~0.09124 m, a drift of only ~0.00024 m from the armed reference -- well inside the 0.01 m effects tolerance, so the object tracked the gripper -- pass. (4) grasp_effort_plateau: the same finger_joint evidence shows the effort plateaued at 57.69, far above the 0.05 air-close floor, confirming physical contact rather than an air grasp -- pass. (5) grasp_width_error_m: I could not evaluate this directly -- the only width-related channel available is the finger_joint position in radians (plateaued at 0.6328), and no registry or contract field gives the radians-to-metres conversion needed to compare against the 0.02 m plausibility band, so this clause is recorded as not evaluable from available evidence rather than guessed. (6) Missed-grasp requirement (instruction-level, no clause_id): the part tracked the gripper the whole carry per the slip monitor and lift evidence, and it is u_brown's own pose that moved and matches u_brown_placement at the end, so the grasp held the intended part, not another -- pass. (7) Final seat check, my own measurement: query_snapshot gives u_brown at (0.40481,-0.14229,0.04336) vs u_brown_placement at (0.40414,-0.14297,0.04538), a position error of ~0.0022 m, within the 0.01 m position tolerance, and orientations match closely -- pass. base1's stationarity monitor (mon_7ea00b09d167) has not fired across this span, so the fixture was undisturbed. Overall: the part is correctly seated, but the clamp-effort invariant stands violated at this milestone, so the step is non_conformant on that clause even though the seating effect itself is good.

payload.explanation: FINAL run-level end-state verdict, covering steps pick_u_brown, place_approach_u_brown, place_u_brown, pick_u_orange, place_approach_u_orange, place_u_orange, pick_line_green, place_approach_line_green, place_line_green, pick_inverted_u_yellow, place_approach_inverted_u_yellow, place_inverted_u_yellow -- all twelve were on the expected process map; no unplanned step_id was ever seen. I measured the end-state myself via query_snapshot after run_ended (status=completed): u_brown at 0.00212 m, u_orange at 0.00208 m, line_green at 0.00804 m, and inverted_u_yellow at 0.00244 m from their respective placement frames, all comfortably within their registry position tolerances (0.01/0.02/0.015/0.012 m respectively), with matching orientations. base1's stationarity monitor (reference captured before the first step) never fired through the whole run, and its final pose is unchanged within noise. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) had stationarity monitors armed before the first step; none fired, and their final poses in this snapshot match their run-start poses within noise, so none was disturbed despite the ACM-permitted carried-part-through-bystander channel being available throughout. No unexpected object or scene event was observed during any look, so no record_observation entries were needed. The one standing non-conformance is u_brown's clamp effort: the invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous monitor (le 10, from registry max_clamp_effort for u_brown) fired at pick_u_brown (24.1) and the effort evidence shows it plateaued and stayed at 48-58 units -- roughly 5-6x the part's own tolerated limit -- continuously from the moment the gripper closed through pick_u_brown, place_approach_u_brown and place_u_brown, until release. This was recorded as a finding at each of those three steps as required. I am not treating this as recovered: the overclamp was never corrected by any subsequent action, it simply ended when the gripper opened at release -- unlike a misseated part that a reseat can fix, there is no action that retroactively makes an already-applied excess clamp force conform, so I do not credit the run with a recovery on this clause. Although u_brown's own final seated position is within tolerance and nothing else in the run was violated, this clause failed and stands as a recorded, uncorrected departure, so per the verdict rule that a standing violation wins regardless of how the run otherwise completed, the final verdict is non_conformant on invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous for u_brown. All other clauses across all four parts, the fixture, and the bystanders passed; effects.grasp_width_error_m could not be evaluated for any of the four parts because the only width-related channel is the finger_joint position in radians and no contract or registry field gives a radians-to-metres conversion for the 0.02 m plausibility band -- this is named as not evaluable rather than guessed, consistently across all four place steps.
